content.intro: This lesson covers Upgrading Dependencies and Migrating Rust Editions. It sits in Module 27, Professional Rust Tooling and Team Workflows, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Upgrading Dependencies and Migrating Rust Editions matters when you work with toolchain choice and reproducibility. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Rust tooling makes the build, dependency graph, formatting, linting, and test steps repeatable. Use the project’s declared toolchain and Cargo metadata rather than relying on undocumented local state.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Upgrading Dependencies and Migrating Rust Editions, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. A professional workflow automates formatting, linting, tests, dependency review, and reproducible builds. Review edition migrations and public API changes before merging.
